safety_boundary: Recovery-only repository threat model covering documentation, configuration, and tests. This register is not an independent external audit and does not authorize or claim consensus-state, cryptography, wallet-custody, key, signing, funds, deployment, mainnet, migration, release, or production activity. The repository holds no secrets, private keys, real topology, or customer data; all committed configuration is synthetic.

assets.description: Canonical bank state, the 21,000,000 PNYX supply cap, module escrow, and treasury accounting.
Domains, proposals, votes, validator claims, stake, and slash state in x/truedemocracy.
DEX pool reserves, provider-owned LP shares, asset registry, and swap burn settlement.
CometBFT validator identity, consensus-key history and revocation, and signer state held by operators, never by the repository.
Pinned genesis verification-key state, identity Merkle roots, and the active nullifier set protecting anonymous voting.
The client-web browser client and user-side key material, which remains user-held and outside repository custody.
The truerepublicd daemon, deterministic build contract, and release artifacts derived from this repository.
GitHub workflows, pinned Actions, dependency lockfiles, and the security gate contract guarding them.
Structured logs, private metrics, dashboards, alert rules, and recovery drill evidence.

actors.description: Unauthenticated remote party probing P2P, RPC, or client-facing surfaces.
Consensus participant that equivocates, censors, goes offline, or is compromised.
Governance, treasury, or DEX user attempting spoofed identity, theft, or arithmetic exploitation.
Configured or intercepted RPC/REST endpoint returning forged or incomplete chain data to the browser client.
Party poisoning dependencies, toolchains, Actions, or build inputs.
Operator whose credentials, signer, or host are partially compromised.
Reviewed repository maintainer acting through protected CI and append-only Bridge records.
Operator running seed, sentry, validator, RPC, or private roles under documented policy.

trust_boundaries.description: Untrusted internet and peer nodes versus sentry-shielded validators with deny-by-default role policy.
data_flows: Consensus votes, proposals, and blocks between validators through sentries
Peer exchange and discovery limited to sanctioned roles
State-sync snapshots from trusted validators to catching-up nodes

trust_boundaries.description: CometBFT consensus versus the Cosmos SDK application over ABCI, including evidence and upgrade boundaries.
data_flows: Deterministic BeginBlock/DeliverTx/EndBlock transitions
ABCI++ misbehavior evidence feeding slashing
Export/import and migration state across binary versions

trust_boundaries.description: Custom governance and DEX modules versus canonical bank custody and the cap-checked issuance service.
data_flows: Escrow, stake, fee, reward, and slash transfers as exact bank movements
DEX reserve settlement and canonical supply burns
Every-block crisis invariants over supply, escrow, reserves, and LP totals

trust_boundaries.description: Client-side proof generation versus the on-chain pinned verification-key boundary; no real prover exists yet.
data_flows: Versioned chain/proposal/rating-bound proof signals
Nullifier publication preventing double votes
Genesis-pinned verification key consulted at vote time

trust_boundaries.description: Browser client versus the configured CometBFT RPC/REST provider, which is trusted for completeness until a light client exists.
data_flows: Registered protobuf gRPC-over-ABCI queries
Centralized simulate/sign/deliver transaction flow
User key material that never leaves user custody

trust_boundaries.description: Maintained source versus CI runners, third-party Actions, and external package registries.
data_flows: SHA-pinned Action execution with read-only permissions
Lockfile-bound Go, Rust, and npm dependency resolution
Fail-closed vulnerability, static-analysis, and secret gates

trust_boundaries.description: Operator-held keys, signer state, and host infrastructure versus the secret-free repository.
data_flows: Generated-key genesis bootstrap writing mode-0600 files
Sanitized backup artifacts excluding key material
Secret-minimized structured logs and private-only metrics

trust_boundaries.description: Future IBC channels versus counterparty chains; currently an explicit non-goal with disabled stubs.
data_flows: No live packet flow exists today
Documented setup guidance remains untested against a second chain

assumptions: Pinned CometBFT, Cosmos SDK, and Wasmd releases behave as specified; reachable upstream vulnerabilities without fixes are tracked with bounded exceptions.
Operators keep private keys, seed phrases, and signer state outside the repository; committed topology and rehearsal data is synthetic only.
The maintained client-web is the single supported public client; retired prototypes exist only in Git history.
Protected GitHub CI on the exact reviewed head is the authoritative public verification signal.
One consensus identity has exactly one active signer under operator custody procedures.
non_goals: Production, mainnet, real-funds, or real-key readiness approval; production_ready is false.
An independent external security audit; this register is repository self-assessment only.
A real Groth16 prover, ceremony artifact, or independent cryptographic review.
Live IBC relaying, two-chain tests, or a public testnet.
Publication of private topology, firewall, DNS, or provider configuration.
Release artifact signing, SBOM, provenance, or publishing.
Browser light-client verification of the configured RPC provider.

threats.attack_path: External attacker eclipses or floods validators through public P2P listeners, peer exchange, or forged topology.
threats.impact: Consensus liveness loss, validator isolation, or deanonymization of the validator set.
controls: GH-71 role-based policy: validators run no public P2P listener, PEX, or seeds and dial at least two sentries
GH-89 cross-node topology qualification with deny-by-default flows and reserved external principal
Fail-closed startup validation of per-role network policy
threats.residual_risk: Repository policy is verified, but no applied firewall, proxy, DNS, or private live topology deployment evidence exists.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 1 exit gate: reproduce topology and recovery results on clean infrastructure

threats.attack_path: A consensus-breaking upgrade or partially applied migration corrupts or splits canonical state with no rehearsed rollback.
threats.impact: Ledger divergence, permanent state loss, or an unrecoverable chain halt.
controls: Compatible binary replacement and fail-before-open rollback drills on persisted validator homes
Bounded fresh-genesis legacy-authority migration with exact export binding
Sanitized backup/restore/export/import drills and every-block crisis invariants
GH-184 immutable-electorate two-thirds governance, old-binary halt, cached-write failure rollback, fixed-candidate recovery, and exact-once four-validator restart
threats.residual_risk: The bounded fresh-genesis v0.4.1 path is locally rehearsed, but pre-GH-184 store introduction, clean private infrastructure reproduction, independent review, and production operation remain unqualified.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 1 exit gate: reproduce the governed upgrade and recovery path on clean private infrastructure and obtain independent review

threats.attack_path: Malicious participant spoofs identity or authority to claim treasury, stake, validator, or registry privileges.
threats.impact: Theft of escrowed funds, unauthorized validator power, or corrupted governance state.
controls: Identity derived only from authenticated signers or verified proofs, never caller-supplied strings
Exact bank escrow backs every domain, proposal, stake, deposit, and withdrawal claim
Chain-authority comparison before asset registry mutation and cached atomic settlement
threats.residual_risk: Merged recovery evidence covers spoofed, duplicate, and injected-failure cases; independent review remains a GH-7 program item, not a repository claim.
threats.next_gate: Preserve signer-bound identity; re-verify under the GH-29 Phase 5 security-depth review

threats.attack_path: Attacker front-runs anonymous rating reward payouts because proof and signature payloads do not bind a safe bank recipient.
threats.impact: Reward theft from anonymous voters and forced deanonymization pressure.
controls: Anonymous rating rewards are deferred; production handlers refuse unsafe direct payout
Proofs and legacy signatures bind chain, domain, issue, suggestion, and rating
The maintained web client fails closed on mock or unsafe submission
threats.residual_risk: No front-running-safe anonymous reward-recipient binding design has passed review.
threats.next_gate: GH-7: design and independently review recipient-bound anonymous rewards before enabling payouts

threats.attack_path: Minting, genesis, or reward logic inflates supply beyond the 21,000,000 PNYX cap or desynchronizes module custody.
threats.impact: Irreversible supply-cap violation and loss of the token's core scarcity invariant.
controls: One canonical cap-checked issuance service reads bank supply before every mint
Bank genesis rejects over-cap supply before any custom module mutation
Every-block crisis invariant halts on supply, escrow, reserve, or LP divergence
threats.residual_risk: Cap, escrow, and custody reconciliation has merged local and CI evidence; it remains recovery evidence, not production approval.
threats.next_gate: Preserve the single issuance boundary; re-verify under GH-29 Phase 5 depth review

threats.attack_path: Malicious participant drains DEX reserves, withdraws foreign LP shares, or mutates the asset registry without authority.
threats.impact: Loss of pooled funds and corrupted market state.
controls: Exact module-bank custody is the only public transition path with cached atomic settlement
Withdrawals require provider-owned LP shares behind length-prefixed keys
Registry and status mutation require the configured chain authority
threats.residual_risk: Custody, slippage, and authority boundaries are regression-tested; independent DEX review stays open under GH-7.
threats.next_gate: Preserve custody-wrapper exclusivity; re-verify under GH-29 Phase 5 depth review

threats.attack_path: Without a real compatible Groth16 prover, any enabled anonymous path would rely on mock or incompatible proofs.
threats.impact: Forged anonymous votes or a false sense of privacy guarantees.
controls: Anonymous submission stays fail-closed in the maintained client and mock proof submission is rejected
Consensus never runs randomized setup; genesis pins circuit ID, VK fingerprint, curve, and public-input shape
Versioned signals bind chain, proposal, and rating context
threats.residual_risk: No real prover, reproducible circuit artifacts, or browser-to-chain real-proof compatibility tests exist; this register claims none.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 2 exit gate: a real maintained-client proof verifies on-chain under the published circuit identity

threats.attack_path: A compromised or unaudited trusted setup or circuit error weakens soundness or leaks voter identity.
threats.impact: Undetectable vote forgery or privacy loss across the anonymity set.
controls: Genesis ceremony artifacts are treated as the trust anchor with pinned fingerprints
Identity roots are recomputed from canonical commitments and nullifier state survives export/import
Enabling any real prover is gated on external review
threats.residual_risk: Ceremony provenance, participant assumptions, and independent cryptographic, privacy, and trusted-setup review are absent and not claimed.
threats.next_gate: GH-7: complete independent cryptographic and trusted-setup review before any prover enablement

threats.attack_path: Enabling IBC on a public counterparty or across an unsupported governed upgrade without qualified relayer and migration evidence can strand or duplicate cross-chain value.
threats.impact: Loss or duplication of PNYX on counterparty chains and unrecoverable channel state.
controls: GH-175, GH-178, and GH-181 provide local proof-driven two-chain packet, channel, and compatible binary-restart recovery evidence
GH-184 provides local governed x/upgrade migration failure and recovery evidence across four validators
External relayers, public counterparties, pre-GH-184 store introduction, and IBC client upgrades remain exit-gated
Public status continues to mark the repository non-production
threats.residual_risk: No external relayer/public-counterparty qualification, pre-GH-184 store transition, or IBC client-upgrade evidence exists.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 3 exit gate: qualify an external relayer/counterparty, pre-existing-chain store transition, and IBC client-upgrade evidence

threats.attack_path: Residual staking or distribution stubs are invoked as if they were supported protocol surfaces.
threats.impact: Undefined consensus behavior or operator confusion about the supported feature boundary.
controls: IBC staking and standard CosmWasm staking/distribution remain explicit stubs; GH-184 replaced the upgrade stub with the real keeper
Limitations and roadmap documents define the exact supported Cosmos boundary
Unsupported surfaces must be absent or unmistakably disabled before rollout
threats.residual_risk: The remaining staking and distribution compatibility stubs are documented but not yet implemented, replaced, or removed.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 3: implement, replace, or explicitly remove remaining stubs and document the boundary

threats.attack_path: Malicious or compromised RPC provider returns forged or incomplete chain data to the browser client.
threats.impact: Users see fabricated governance, DEX, or history state and may sign against false information.
controls: Client uses only registered protobuf gRPC-over-ABCI paths and fails closed on malformed responses
Typed unavailable, timeout, protocol, and decode states never fabricate empty state
Chain failure output is control-character-stripped and length-capped
threats.residual_risk: The configured RPC provider remains trusted for completeness; no browser light client or participant index exists.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 4: qualify browser trust boundaries before rollout UX approval

threats.attack_path: Browser key custody weaknesses expose user keys through storage, UI, or signing-flow flaws.
threats.impact: Irreversible theft of user funds without any chain-side fault.
controls: One exact fail-closed transaction registry with a centralized simulate/sign/deliver boundary
Browser quality matrix never submits forms, unlocks stored material, or enters seed phrases
Retired prototypes with unsafe seed-phrase handling are removed from release paths
threats.residual_risk: No independent wallet custody or cryptographic review of the maintained client exists and none is claimed.
threats.next_gate: GH-7: independent wallet and custody review before any authenticated real-funds flow

threats.attack_path: An operator misses consensus, slashing, or capacity incidents because paging, SLOs, and live monitoring are unproven.
threats.impact: Extended liveness loss or undetected validator misbehavior during a real incident.
controls: Immutable Grafana dashboard, eleven deterministic alert rules, and recovery/testnet objectives
Separate bounded liveness and synchronization-aware readiness probes
Incident-command contract with eight synthetic rehearsal scenarios
threats.residual_risk: External paging, production SLOs, private live operator rehearsal, and capacity soak evidence remain open.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 6: complete paging drills, private rehearsal, and soak evidence

threats.attack_path: Logs, metrics, or committed configuration leak credentials, keys, or private transaction material.
threats.impact: Secret disclosure enabling validator or operator compromise.
controls: Secret-minimized structured JSON logging through the central SDK/CometBFT logger boundary
Defensive redaction of reviewed credential, key, and private-transaction patterns
Fail-closed maintained-tree secret scanning with exact synthetic-only exceptions
threats.residual_risk: Redaction covers reviewed patterns; novel secret shapes remain a scanning-residual accepted under the weekly gate cadence.
threats.next_gate: Preserve fail-closed secret gates; re-verify under GH-29 Phase 6 operations review

threats.attack_path: A reachable dependency vulnerability without an upstream fix is merged or left untracked.
threats.impact: Exploitable node, contract, or client behavior inherited from upstream code.
controls: govulncheck, cargo-audit, and high-severity npm audit gates fail closed
No-fix Go findings are allowed only by exact IDs with 30-day-bounded expiry
Dependabot maintenance is grouped minor/patch-only with separately reviewed exceptions
threats.residual_risk: Four reachable no-fix Go findings and monitored cargo-audit warnings remain visible until upstream publishes fixes.
threats.next_gate: Re-validate exceptions inside the 30-day expiry bound; escalate to GH-29 if a fix or exploit appears

threats.attack_path: Supply-chain attacker retargets a mutable Action, persists checkout credentials, or bypasses scanner failures in CI.
threats.impact: Compromised build, test, or release pipeline producing untrustworthy artifacts.
controls: Every third-party Action is pinned to a reviewed full commit SHA with a version comment
Workflows use contents-read permissions, per-job timeouts, and disabled credential persistence
Repository contract rejects mutable references, failure bypasses, and unapproved pins
threats.residual_risk: Pin integrity is enforced by contract test; runner compromise outside repository control is not covered.
threats.next_gate: Preserve SHA pinning and read-only permissions; re-verify under GH-29 Phase 7 release review

threats.attack_path: Unsigned release artifacts without SBOM or provenance are substituted between build and operator installation.
threats.impact: Operators run attacker-controlled binaries believing they are reviewed releases.
controls: Deterministic Linux daemon build contract reproduces artifacts byte-for-byte
Reproducible-build CI compares independent builds before any release claim
Signing, SBOM, provenance, and publishing stay explicitly outside current gates
threats.residual_risk: No artifact signing, SBOM, provenance, or publishing pipeline exists and none is claimed.
threats.next_gate: GH-29 Phase 7: implement artifact signing, SBOM, and provenance before any release

threats.attack_path: Non-deterministic build inputs cause reviewed source and shipped binaries to diverge silently.
threats.impact: Review evidence no longer covers the artifact operators actually run.
controls: Pinned toolchains and a repository-owned deterministic build script
Reproducible Linux build evidence recorded for merged release candidates
Exact dependency lockfiles bound into the security gate contract
threats.residual_risk: Determinism is proven for the Linux daemon target only; other artifact classes remain uncovered until Phase 7.
threats.next_gate: Extend deterministic coverage to remaining artifact classes under GH-29 Phase 7
